segmenti.tekst: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.

قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds, Lord of the Day of Judgment. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: “All the children of Adam are sinners,
all people sin, and the best among the sinners are those who repent much.” From this hadith we can conclude that every person sins.
That every person sins. There is no person who does not err, who does not commit a sin. But the difference is in… the difference is in tawbah, repentance,
and in the effort, the effort of a person to reform himself, his condition.
So that we do not come to a situation where we say: “My Lord, why did this strike me? Why did this calamity hit me? What was this?” What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in the Qur'an?

“وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ” – and whatever sins you commit… that is, the calamity that strikes you, or the misfortune that strikes you, is because of your sins,
because of your sins. And much of it Allah pardons, because He is the Most Merciful. So, the bad things that happen to us – the sabab, or cause, is our sins, my dear brothers.

That is why a person should be careful how he behaves, what he does, and, by Allah, especially what he says, because with words he can do much more harm, well, than with his deeds. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say: “Inna al-'abda layatakallamu bil-kalimati la yara biha ba'san yahwi biha fi nari jahannama sab'ina kharifan” – he said: a person will utter a word without paying attention to it, thinking it is not dangerous, and because of it he will be thrown for 70 autumns, or 70 years, into the Fire of Jahannam (Hellfire).
So the cause of his stay in the Fire for 70 years is – what, dear brothers? Sins have their consequences. Every sin has a consequence.
And the greatest consequence is distance from Allah. And the greatest punishment for a person is that he becomes distant from Allah. There is no greater calamity for him.

So a person stands in prayer – the one who sins a lot and does not repent, does not reform himself – and he does not feel the sweetness, he does not feel the ladhdhah (delight). There is no delight. He stretches out his hands toward the heavens –

it doesn't flow, there is no delight. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: “Al-yawma nansakum kama nasitum liqa'a yawmikum hadha” – it will be said: “Today We will forget you, as you forgot the day of meeting,” that is, the Day of Judgment. So the person who sins a lot is not aware that Allah sees him, is not aware that he will meet Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will disregard him on the Day of Judgment.
Disregard him. Also, among the consequences of sin is that a person's heart becomes hard, that it becomes a heart of stone. What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say?
He said: “In the chest there is a lump, a lump of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is diseased, the whole body is diseased – and that is the heart.”
And that is the heart. Why did the Banu Isra'il, or the Children of Israel, or the Jews…

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, describes in the Qur'an hearts of stone. Because they sinned, because they consumed usury, killed prophets. The Prophet says… Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Then their hearts became like stone, or even harder than stone.”

Why? Because of their sins. And you will see a person who sins a lot, who is disobedient to Allah: it is all the same to him, dear brothers. He doesn't care that there are casinos in the city. He doesn't care that there is corruption.

He doesn't care that there is… that there is immorality. He doesn't care about what is happening in Gaza, what is happening to Muslims in Sudan. It's all the same to him, it's all the same to him. His daughter wants to go out at 11 at night, at 12,

and come back at 1, 2 – he doesn't care, it doesn't interest him. His daughter wants to go out for coffee with male colleagues – to him it's simply… His heart is so stony that he feels neither protective jealousy, nor pangs of conscience, nothing.

That is the punishment for such people. Also, dear brothers, among the things, that is, the consequences of sinning, is, dear brothers, constriction in the chest. Those people who sin constantly have some kind of anxiety in their chest.

So they take him to the imam, then to a fifth one, then to a ninth one, then ruqyah, then this, then… Not everything is about ruqyah, dear brothers. Today, whatever happens to us, people say: “Take him to the imam to recite ruqyah over him.” Has that person changed anything in his life? He hasn't changed anything, he hasn't changed anything in his life.
He won't change. You can take him to whomever you want, but there is no salvation for him until the person himself analyzes his life and returns to the right path. There is no cure for him.
A person is his own cure. Also, among the consequences of sinning are family problems. There are always problems there, family problems.

Allah takes away from a person the blessing of family. As we said, he is not interested in his family, nor his wife, nor his children, nothing interests him. Why? Because Allah has taken away his delight. He has taken away his delight.

Also, among the consequences of sinning is the curse: the curse of Allah, the curse of the prophets, the angels and all people. Allah reports, informs, mentions the Banu Isra'il, or the Jews. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: “Lu'ina alladhina kafaru min Bani Isra'ila 'ala lisani Dawuda wa 'Isa ibni Maryam.”
Cursed were the Children of Israel by the tongue of Dawud and Isa, alayhimus-salam. Why? Because they sinned, because they were great sinners and attacked others unjustly.
And what else? He says: they did not forbid what was bad, the bad things that were in their communities; they did not forbid those things.

Today we have a big problem, dear brothers: when an imam says something from the hutba (Friday sermon), points out some problem in the community, they drag him through the media: “He's like this, and he's like this, and he's like that.

He has no right to talk about politics, he has no right to interfere.” We would like the communist times to return, when the imam was “that and nothing more”: he just comes to the mihrab, well, to pray, with ten old men behind him, half on chairs, half in the first row, and that's it.
We, we would like… that is, not you, but those who run the state, [unclear] and so on. It is necessary, dear brothers, to point out… problems must be pointed out.
The hallmark of the ummah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam – He says: “Kuntum khayra ummatin ukhrijat lin-nas” – you are the best generation, the best people.
Why? You command good and forbid evil; you command good, and you forbid that evil be done.
If I, from this mihrab or minbar, and you in the row… what would we have achieved then? We would have achieved nothing, dear brothers. Should we not talk about the problem of pollution in our city?

Is it impossible to solve? It can be solved, we all know it can be solved. Can the problem of corruption be solved? It can. Of party-based employment? It can. Can it be solved? It can. An example is Bosnia, we saw a few… It can, everything is possible when there is the will. But [unclear] they say: “Efendi, don't,” they say, “interfere in politics. That's not your business.” The Messenger of Allah was a statesman, a statesman, let's say a president [unclear].

And he was a religious leader. And Abu Bakr as well, Umar as well, Uthman as well, Ali as well. But we want to put the imams in a pen a bit, so that they don't dare to say anything. That's what we want.
Also, among the things, the consequences of sin, is, is precisely collective punishment, collective punishment, when people do not command good and do not forbid evil.

You know that hadith, you have probably all heard it: when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sends angels to punish a people, sends angels to punish a people, the angels return to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and say: “There is one man among that people,

there is one man who worships only You, who prostrates to You.” Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Start with him first.” Why? Because he only looked after himself, he did not look after others, he did not command good and forbid evil.

What is his role? What is our role, we who come to the mosque? Our role ends at the door. When we leave the mosque, we rarely call to good and forbid evil. When we work in some places where we can do a lot of good – what do we do?
We do nothing. Little. There is little benefit. A person must look at all of this, because he will be asked, especially about the things he could have prevented.

They will pass, dear brothers, the powerful and the powerless, we will all pass. But one should fear Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also, among the things, that is, the consequences of sin, of sin, is that a person stays up late at night, that he cannot sleep.

So we see a person… this does not refer to students who study, who make an effort… a person turns on a reality show and watches until 2 or 3 o'clock. Also, among the consequences is, is that a person has no peaceful sleep, no peaceful sleep, so he keeps waking up. Also, among the consequences of sin is that a person does not come to the fajr prayer. By Allah, the two most beautiful prayers are fajr and isha in congregation. There are no more beautiful prayers. So woe to the one who does not pray them, especially in congregation.

Also, among the consequences is that a person sleeps for a long time. Barakah (blessing) is in the early hours. A person… [unclear]. There are people who sleep until two, three o'clock, and there is no barakah from him. Also, among the consequences of sinning is that a person has no barakah in [unclear],

and that his provision decreases every day. There is no, no provision. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? He says: whoever fears, whoever fears Allah, Allah will give him a way out of every situation and will provide for him from where he does not expect. And as for the one, by Allah, who does not fear Allah, who constantly [unclear] sins, Allah will take away from him the rizq (provision) that He gave him, and Allah is able, Allah is able to do all things. “Innallaha 'ala kulli shay'in qadir” – indeed, Allah is All-Powerful.

That is why, dear brothers, it is up to a person to constantly analyze his deeds, what he says, what he does, and to repent again and again, because Allah truly, truly loves, loves such people. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive us our sins, to make us among those who constantly… who constantly repent, who constantly… who constantly reform their condition.

I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah (Paradise), to unite us in Jannah with the prophets, with the martyrs, with the righteous servants [unclear]. Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'an al-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi min al-ayati wadh-dhikr al-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwa al-Ghafur ar-Rahim.
